title: Gletcher Aging: Aged to Perfection
description: Two Years of Aging, French Oak and Cognac Barrels: The Story of CYNIC

blocks.html:
Some beers are brewed to quench your thirst. Others are made to tell a story.

Gletcher Brewery introduces a new chapter in its history — Gletcher Aging, a series in which time becomes one of the most important ingredients and the oak barrel becomes a vessel for transformation.

Gletcher Aging is our interpretation of slow brewing.

Unlike conventional beers designed to be consumed soon after production, beers in this series are given time to mature naturally and develop in close contact with wood.

There are no shortcuts here. No artificial flavourings, no attempts to imitate the effects of long maturation. Just beer, noble oak, time and the experience of our brewing team.

The result is a range of complex, evolving beers whose character cannot be rushed.

These are beers for slow drinking, cellaring and special occasions.

And the first release in the series is CYNIC — Gletcher's barrel-aged Russian Imperial Stout.
🍷 Why CYNIC Is More Than Just a Stout

The name CYNIC was chosen deliberately.

On one level, it refers to the world of classical philosophy admired during the age of Catherine the Great. On another, it evokes Diogenes, the ancient Cynic philosopher remembered in popular tradition for choosing an radically independent life in a barrel.

That contrast lies at the heart of the beer itself.

CYNIC brings together two seemingly opposite worlds: the splendour of Imperial Russia and the uncompromising simplicity of ancient philosophy.

It also creates a bridge between history and modern craft brewing.

Russian Imperial Stout traces its heritage to the powerful dark ales brewed in Britain for export to the Russian imperial court in the eighteenth century. CYNIC takes that historical idea and reinterprets it through long maturation, oak and the character of former spirit barrels.

Producing CYNIC took approximately two years.

Its recipe was built around carefully selected European ingredients chosen to provide enough depth and structure for prolonged maturation.

Malt
German Pale Ale malt forms the foundation of the beer, while Belgian Cara 120 and Special B contribute layers of caramel, dark fruit and rich malt character.

Texture and Colour
Oat malt gives the stout its smooth, velvety mouthfeel.
Highly roasted malts reaching 900–1200 EBC provide its deep colour and characteristic notes of roasted coffee, bitter chocolate and a subtle suggestion of smoke.

Hops
German Magnum delivers a clean bitterness that balances the intensity of the malt.
Slovenian Aurora and Bobek add elegant herbal and spicy nuances without overwhelming the beer's darker character.
⏳ The Magic of Maturation: Cognac and Limousin Oak

A crucial stage in CYNIC's evolution began in June 2023.

The beer first spent 365 days in a fermentation tank, allowing its structure and tannic character to develop gradually.

The next transformation began in July 2024, when CYNIC was transferred into barrels made from French oak originating in the Limousin region.

And these were far from ordinary barrels.

Before receiving the stout, they had spent around 25 years maturing premium spirits for the Kuban Cognac House.

Another year inside these barrels profoundly changed the beer.

The oak softened its structure and introduced elegant woody tones, while the barrels' previous life added another dimension: dried fruit, mature spirit character and a delicate trace of tobacco smoke.

The result is not simply a stronger stout, but a beer whose flavour has been shaped by time, wood and everything the barrel carried before it.

A beer like CYNIC deserves the same attention you might give to a mature wine or fine spirit.

To experience its full range of aromas and flavours, a few details matter.

Choose the right glass.
A snifter or a large wine glass works especially well, allowing the aromas to collect above the surface of the beer.

Don't serve it too cold.
The recommended serving temperature is around 12–16°C. As the beer warms, chocolate, cognac, roasted malt, fruit and spice become increasingly expressive.

Take your time.
CYNIC is not designed to be rushed. Take a small sip, allow the beer to warm on the palate and notice how its velvety texture develops into a long, warming finish.

The beer will continue to evolve in the glass — and potentially in the bottle as well.

CYNIC was created with long-term cellaring in mind.

For collectors, there is a simple way to turn a case into a six-year tasting experiment.

Buy a case of six bottles and open one bottle on the same date every year.

Over time, the beer will change. Some flavours will soften, others may become deeper and more integrated, while entirely new nuances can emerge through bottle maturation.

After six years, you will have experienced your own vertical tasting — six different stages in the evolution of the same beer.

It turns every bottle into an event and transforms the act of cellaring into part of the experience itself.

CYNIC is produced in limited quantities for collectors, enthusiasts and anyone who believes that some things are worth waiting for.

Time does not simply preserve this beer. It becomes part of it.
CYNIC marks the beginning of the Gletcher Aging series and a new direction for Gletcher Brewery — beers created not for speed, but for depth, transformation and time.
